outcome: A preprint by Dutour Sikirić and van Woerden (arXiv:2508.20719) computes all 2,237,251,040 perfect lattices in dimension 9 via Voronoi's algorithm and derives that the Hermite constant γ9 equals 2, extending the set of dimensions with a known value beyond {1-8, 24} for the first time since 24 was settled. The result has not yet received independent expert digestion, journal acceptance, or independent reproduction of the computation.
summary: The Wikipedia bullet asserts the Hermite constant is known only for dimensions 1-8 and 24. The triage pointer was correct: a preprint posted 28 August 2025 (revised 7 February 2026) by Mathieu Dutour Sikirić and Wessel van Woerden, 'The lattice packing problem in dimension 9 by Voronoi's algorithm' (arXiv:2508.20719), completes Voronoi's algorithm in dimension 9 for the first time, enumerating all 2,237,251,040 perfect lattices up to similarity, and concludes as a corollary that γ9 = 2 (with the laminated lattice Λ9 achieving the densest packing). This is squarely a case of the stated problem (it fills in exactly the 'dimensions other than 1-8 and 24' the bullet names), not a variant, so it counts under §3.1. I read the full text (via the arXiv HTML rendering) and confirmed the methodology is entirely classical: Voronoi's 1908 algorithm, graph-isomorphism software (Nauty/Traces), polyhedral computation libraries (PPL, LRS), and MPI-parallelized enumeration, with completeness certified by the algorithm's own termination criterion (no new perfect-form neighbors found) and a consistency check against a prior partial enumeration for high-incidence forms. No machine learning, neural network, or other AI system is mentioned anywhere in the text or acknowledgements, so ai_role is 'none'. I classified status as 'claimed' rather than 'resolved': the paper remains an arXiv preprint with no journal submission/acceptance noted, and I found no expert digestion (no Terence Tao or comparable blog treatment, no citing survey, no independent reproduction of the 2.2-billion-lattice enumeration) as of my search on 2026-09-22 — only the authors' own account and secondary paraphrases of the abstract. The 'directly checkable by computer algebra' clause of the resolved definition is a genuine complication: the computation is deterministic and the authors' code/data are on Zenodo, so a suitably resourced expert could rerun it, but no evidence I found shows anyone has done so, and a computation of this scale is not 'directly checkable by hand' in the way the rule seems to intend for a quick verification. I therefore treat it as claimed rather than resolved, pending independent confirmation.
competing_reading: One could argue for 'resolved' on the grounds that the result rests on a deterministic, reproducible enumeration algorithm (not a probabilistic or heuristic method) with data published on Zenodo, so it is 'directly checkable ... by computer algebra' per the resolved criterion even without a human having independently redone it. Under that reading the status would be 'resolved', direction 'confirmed', with ai_role and all other fields unchanged.
what_would_settle_it: An independent reproduction or audit of the dimension-9 perfect-lattice enumeration (or of the derived γ9 = 2 claim) by another group, a journal acceptance, or a digestion by a recognized expert commentator (e.g., a blog post, survey, or update to the Hermite constant / sphere-packing literature citing and endorsing the result) would move this to 'resolved'.
